annotations.title: Who leaue the right way.
annotations.text: Generally this description of vvicked men, agreeth to al that committe and persist in mortal sinne, vvhether they vvalked right at anie time before or no; but most especially shevveth the properties of heretikes: <mn>[1]</mn> vvho forsake and leaue the direct, ancient, beaten, knovvne vvay of the Catholique Church, <mn>[2]</mn> and teach nevv obscure doctrines, not heard of, or not approued in our forefathers time. <mn>[3]</mn> Secondly (v. 14) they glorie in their ovvne deuises, and reioyce in most vvicked thinges, as in seducing multitude of peoples, to rebel against their Catholique Princes, and other Superiors spiritual and temporal, in breaking vovves; in despising good vvorkes; trusting to only faith, and that not the Catholique faith of al true Christians, but euerie one his particular persvvasion, that himself is iust, & shal be saued, vvhich by their ovvne doctrin, none is bond to beleue of an others state, but of his ovvne only. In so much that the chiefest point of a Protestants imagined faith, is not a general Article, vvhich al do or should beleue, but a most particular and singular phantasie, vvhich each one must conceiue of himself, or herself. <mn>[4]</mn> Thirdly (v. 16.) Heresie, called here the strange and forrene vvoman, tempereth her vvordes, to please the itching eares of her auditorie, framing her doctrine to the humour of those, vvhom she seeketh to peruert. The same vvhich the Apostle saith in other vvordes, by svveete speaches and benedictions they seduce the hartes of innocents. <mn>[5]</mn> Fourthly (v. 19.) Those that do enter into error of heresie, shal not returne, that is, very hardly and rarely returne into the right vvay of life; <mn>[6]</mn> the reason vvhereof the same Apostle yeldeth, because an heretike is condemned by his ovvne iudgement. <mn>[7]</mn> For being in error, and admitting no iudge but himself, he parteth from the Church, excludeth the meanes of better instruction, & through his erronious iudgement, remaineth in damnable opinion, and so in the state of damnation.

notes.text: Foure markes of an heretike. 1. He forsaketh the knowen faith.
2. He glorieth in his ovvne inuention.
